{{Short description|67th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1998 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 8 March – 25 July 1998 |teams = 33 |team1 = Cork |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 14th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= Kerry |three = Mayo |previous = [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] |next = [[1999 National Hurling League|1999]] }} The '''1998 National Hurling League''' (known as the '''[[Allianz|Church & General]] National Hurling League''') was the 67th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1998 |winners=[[Cork GAA|Cork]]

(3 May 1998) |highest scoring=[[Clare GAA|Clare]] 3-21 - 2-7 [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]
(8 March 1988) |matches= 33 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] |nextseason=[[1999 National Hurling League|1999]] |updated=10 March 2017 }} The league saw a major restructuring of the usual four divisions of eight teams. Division 1 was split into Group 1A and Group 1B with each group consisting of six teams. The top two teams in each group qualified for the knock-out stage. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1997 National Hurling League|1997 season]]. [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], [[Cork GAA|Cork]], [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] all entered Division 1 as part of the restructuring. On 17 May 1998, Cork won the title after a 2–14 to 0–13 win over Waterford in the final. It was their 14th league title overall and their first since [[1992-93 National Hurling League|1992-93]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} Cork's [[Joe Deane]] was the Division 1 top scorer with 3-30. ===Division 1A table=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: centre;" !width=20|Pos !width=150|Team !width=20|Pld !width=20|W !width=20|D !width=20|L !width=40|F !width=40|A !width=20|Diff !width=20|Pts !width=250|Notes |- style |'''1'''||align=left|''' [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] '''||'''5'''||'''5'''||'''0'''||'''0'''||'''7-57'''||'''4-58'''||'''18'''||'''10''' |- style |'''2'''||align=left|''' [[Clare GAA|Clare]] '''||'''5'''||'''3'''||'''0'''||'''2'''||'''5-83'''||'''9-52'''||'''19'''||'''6''' |- style |'''3'''||align=left|''' [[Galway GAA|Galway]] '''||'''5'''||'''3'''||'''0'''||'''2'''||'''9-67'''||'''4-66'''||'''16'''||'''6''' |- style |'''4'''||align=left|''' [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] '''||'''5'''||'''2'''||'''0'''||'''3'''||'''8-59'''||'''5-62'''||'''6'''||'''4''' |- style |'''5'''||align=left|''' [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] '''||'''5'''||'''1'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''6-62'''||'''10-58'''||'''-8'''||'''2''' |- style |'''6'''||align=left|''' [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] '''||'''5'''||'''1'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''7-47'''||'''9-49'''||'''-8'''||'''2''' |} ===Group stage=== {{football box collapsible |date = 8 March 1998 |team1 = [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |score = 1-13 - Division 2 was split into Group 2A and Group 2B with each group consisting of seven teams. The top two teams in each group qualified for the knock-out stage. [[Armagh GAA|Armagh]], [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]], [[Derry GAA|Derry]], [[Down GAA|Down]], [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]], [[Louth GAA|Louth]], [[Monaghan GAA|Monaghan]], [[Roscommon GAA|Roscommon]], [[Tyrone GAA|Tyrone]] and [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] all entered Division 1 as part of the restructuring. On 25 July 1998, [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] won the title after a 1–11 to 2–6 win over [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] in a replay of the final. It was their 5th Division 2 league title overall and their first since [[1967-68 National Hurling League|1967-68]]. ===Division 2A table=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: centre;"
